Job Title:
Entry-Level Robotics Test Engineer - Navigation
Location:
Atlanta, GA
Employment Type:
Full-time (on-site)
About the job
We are seeking a Robotics Test Engineer to support the testing, validation, and continuous improvement of our autonomous robotic navigation systems. This role will focus on algorithm testing, software release validation, and map optimization. The ideal candidate has a foundational understanding of robotics, strong analytical skills, and an interest in autonomous navigation technologies. This role provides hands-on experience in comprehensive robotic system testing, covering a wide range of software, algorithms, and system functionalities. The engineer will collaborate with cross-functional engineering teams to evaluate and improve overall system performance, reliability, and stability.
Minimum Qualifications
• Bachelor’s degree or above, in Robotics, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Mechanical Engineering or a related field.
• Basic coding skills in one or more programming languages (C++ and Python are strongly preferred).
• Ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
• Strong sense of responsibility, willingness to learn, and ability to quickly grasp new technical concepts and apply them in a hands-on, collaborative environment.
• Hands-on experience with MATLAB and ROS/ROS 2 through academic projects, internships, or professional experience.
Essential Requirements
• Ability to travel to or commute between client’s project locations as needed.
• Willingness to temporarily work at alternative sites during training periods or until assigned facility is operational.
• Travel frequency will vary based on business needs and operational status of assigned facility.
Preferred Qualifications
• Familiarity with autonomous mobile robots (AMRs), automated guided vehicles (AGVs), or other autonomous robotic systems.
• Basic understanding of robotic navigation, localization, mapping, SLAM, or motion control.
• Experience with robotics testing, debugging, data analysis, or technical documentation through academic projects, research, or internships.
• Familiarity with NVIDIA Isaac Sim or similar robotics simulation platforms is preferred.
About VisionNav® Robotics USA
Headquarters in Atlanta, VisionNav® Robotics is a global leader in autonomous industrial vehicles (AMRs/AGVs) and logistics automation solutions. By combining deep learning, environmental perception, and servo control technologies, VisionNav has built nine product series that support a wide range of material handling applications. With over 750 projects delivered in more than 30 countries, VisionNav is trusted by numerous Fortune 500 companies across automotive, food and beverage, chemicals, pharmaceuticals, and 3PL. At VisionNav, we are committed to helping customers build safer, smarter, and more efficient operations through advanced automation.
Key Responsibilities
• Conduct simulation-based and real-world testing of robotic algorithms developed by the North American R & D team to verify their performance under various testing conditions.
• Design and execute test cases, collect and analyze test data, identify potential issues, and prepare detailed technical test reports.
• Collaborate closely with algorithm engineers to investigate technical issues, support algorithm optimization, and perform follow-up testing to verify improvements.
• Perform functional, integration, and regression testing of robotic navigation systems and simulation platforms prior to major software releases to ensure system stability and reliability.
• Identify, document, and track software defects, communicate findings to relevant engineering teams, and verify issue resolution through retesting.
• Assist with map validation and optimization, identifying potential mapping issues and supporting improvements to navigation and localization performance.
• Work with cross-functional engineering teams to support comprehensive robotic system testing, troubleshoot technical issues, and contribute to continuous improvements in system performance and reliability.
U.S. Benefits
Medical insurance, 401(k), PTO.

Title: Cloud Infrastructure Engineer
Location: White Plains, NY (3 days onsite)

About Cogent Infotech
At Cogent Infotech, we believe in creating opportunities that empower individuals and transform organizations. With over 23 years of excellence in consulting and talent solutions, we pride ourselves on building inclusive workplaces and driving innovation in everything we do. Our diverse teams bring unique perspectives to help deliver cutting-edge solutions to global clients across both public and private sectors.
Position Summary
This Cloud Infrastructure Engineer role will participate in designs, builds, and maintenance of scalable foundations for cloud applications and infrastructure. They will collaborate across NYPA IT daily to implement Infrastructure as Code (IaC), manage and provision systems and services, and optimize costs and security across major platforms like Amazon Web Services (AWS), Microsoft Azure, or Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

Maintain consistency across environments by using immutable infrastructure principles, reducing deployment drift.

Set up proactive monitoring, logging, and alerting using tools like Datadog, CloudWatch, or Prometheus.
Participate in on-call rotations to support production services, perform root cause analysis, and handle routine maintenance.
Required Qualifications and Skills
College Degree Cloud and systems related certifications.
Cloud Platform Mastery (AWS, Azure, or GCP).
Infrastructure as Code (Terraform, Ansible).
Containerization (Docker, Kubernetes, Openshift).
Strong foundational knowledge of networking, Windows, and Linux systems.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/43390.description_preview:
About Reducto
Reducto is the agentic document platform for leading AI teams who demand enterprise performance at scale. We provide a comprehensive toolkit for working with documents the way a human would, combining custom in-house and leading frontier models to power efficient and accurate document workflows.
We’ve grown rapidly, increasing revenue 8x year over year and partnering with hundreds of companies, from leading AI teams like Harvey, Vanta, and Scale, to enterprise customers across FAANG and top trading firms.
Reducto has raised over $100M from world-class investors including a16z, Benchmark, and First Round Capital.
The Role
As a Product Engineer, you'll work on the features used by our customers to design, build, test, and evaluate their business critical document workflows. Our goal is to make document data accessible to anyone, technical or not. We aim to build a end-to-end product suite that starts from where your documents are stored all the way to exporting the parsed and extracted data to where you want to use it. You'll work on everything from interactive document viewers to data extraction workflows, building delightful experiences that make complex AI capabilities feel simple.
We Would Love To Meet You If You:
Philosophy: You are your own worst critic. You have a high bar for quality and don't rest until the job is done right—no settling for 90%. We want someone who ships fast, with high agency, and who doesn't just voice problems but actively jumps in to fix them.
Product Intuition: You have a sharp eye for what good product looks like and how it's built. You care about the details that matter and think with first principles.
Experience: You have 2+ years of experience building applications with modern frameworks.
Language/Skills: You're exceptional at TypeScript and React, with strong design sensibility. You understand both the technical and visual aspects of great product experiences.
Tools: Build your own tools as needed—like a quick prototype to test a new interaction pattern or a component library to speed up development.
Approach: A quantitative approach to building products. Ability to debug, experiment, and iterate fast. You should be comfortable getting hands-on with the full development lifecycle, from ideation to shipping to users.
The Core Work Will Include:
Building and refining Reducto Studio's core features—document viewers, extraction workflows, data visualization, and editing interfaces
Creating delightful, intuitive UIs that elegantly decomposes complex document workflows
Ideating, prototyping and iteratively delivering new features like form filling, translations, document editing and document classification
Implementing real-time collaboration features and responsive interfaces that work seamlessly across devices
Working within our design system and stack (Next.js, Tailwind, Convex) to ship fast while maintaining high quality
Experimenting with new interaction patterns to make AI-powered document processing feel magical
Working directly with the founders and customers to shape the product direction based on user feedback
Bonus Points If You:
Have prior experience founding a company or building products at early stages
Have experience with document viewers, PDF rendering, or complex data visualization
Are ambitious and driven, and care a lot about doing great work with great people
Keep up with the latest developments in frontend engineering and design systems
This is an in person role at our office in SF. We're an early stage company which means that the role requires working hard and moving quickly. Please only apply if that excites you.
About Reducto
Nearly 80% of enterprise data is in unstructured formats like PDFs
PDFs are the status quo for enterprise knowledge in nearly every industry. Insurance claims, financial statements, invoices, and health records are all stored in a structure that’s simply impractical for use in digital workflows. This isn’t an inconvenience—it’s a critical bottleneck that leads to dozens of wasted hours every week.
Traditional approaches fail at reliably extracting information in complex PDFs
OCR and even more sophisticated ML approaches work for simple text documents but are unreliable for anything more complex. Text from different columns are jumbled together, figures are ignored, and tables are a nightmare to get right. Overcoming this usually requires a large engineering effort dedicated to building specialized pipelines for every document type you work with.
Reducto Breaks Document Layouts Into Subsections And Then Contextually Parses Each Depending On The Type Of Content. This Is Made Possible By a Combination Of Vision Models, LLMs, And a Suite Of Heuristics We Built Over Time. Put Simply, We Can Help You:
Accurately extract text and tables even with nonstandard layouts
Automatically convert graphs to tabular data and summarize images in documents
Extract important fields from complex forms with simple, natural language instructions
Build powerful retrieval pipelines using Reducto’s document metadata
Intelligently chunk information using the document’s layout data
Benefits at Reducto
At Reducto, we’re invested in the well-being and growth of our team. Here’s what we currently offer:
Unlimited PTO: We believe great work requires recharging.
Lunch: Receive a free lunch to eat with your teammates daily at the office
Reimbursed Transportation: Provide us with your receipts and we’ll take care of the costs
Insurance: Generous health insurance covering medical, dental, and vision.
Health and Wellness Budget: We provide up to $150/mo reimbursement for health and wellness spending, such as gym memberships, fitness classes, or similar.
Parental Leave: Work with us to build a leave schedule that works for you and your family

We are Built to Connect.

Job Overview
T-Mobile Home Internet is one of our fastest growing businesses, and the software this team builds runs on every gateway and mesh extender we put in a customer's home. We're a small development team on a large program, so you'll contribute to meaningful software development work from the start.
You'll develop the device agents that manage, monitor, and troubleshoot our broadband customer premises equipment. They're written in C and C++ against the Broadband Forum's open USP standards and run on the RDK-B platform. The agent uses a microservice architecture, and you'll develop and maintain assigned services within the established architecture.
Your agents will interface with the device's Wi-Fi and cellular subsystems through RDK and RBUS. You won't be writing Wi-Fi drivers or modem firmware, but understanding those technologies, and how RDK components talk to each other, is central to doing this job well.
What You'll Do
Develop and maintain one or more microservices within the device management agent, in C and C++ on RDK-B.
Implement and maintain device data model parameters and USP protocol behavior across supported hardware platforms.
Interface with the device's Wi-Fi and cellular subsystems through RDK and RBUS to configure them, query state, and report it upstream.
Build and maintain the containerized services that run on the device, delivered through a Kubernetes-based packaging and deployment pipeline.
Write unit tests for new and changed code and extend our automated test coverage.
Debug across the device software stack, from log analysis and root cause investigation through to fix verification.
Support device maintenance releases, including test support, firmware validation, and release verification.
Work with OEM partners on defect triage and reproduction.
Improve how we collect data and logs from the field so issues can be triaged and resolved faster.
Contribute ideas that improve how we build, test, and deliver device software.
Document your code, the data model and device behavior.

Description
Amazon Robotics is looking for an experienced Systems Development Engineer to join the Imperium Data Services team in Austin. Data Services owns the source-of-truth data behind network automation across Amazon's fulfillment network: what devices exist, where they live, how they should be configured, which credentials they use, and what state they are actually in. Our services handle nearly a billion API calls a month and sit underneath config generation, deployment, and lifecycle workflows for hundreds of thousands of IP-enabled devices across thousands of sites. When our data is wrong, networks break; when it is right and fast, the rest of automation can run with confidence.
In this role you will partner with software, systems, and network engineers around the world to build and operate the data layer that network automation depends on. You will work on high-throughput APIs and data stores, collection of live device state, data pipelines, and the validation and staging gates that stop bad data before it reaches production devices. Network engineers and automation teams rely on the accuracy of what we serve. Your work will let them get answers in seconds and spend their time on hard problems instead of manual data cleanup. We value correctness, simplicity, and operational excellence in our designs.
Key job responsibilities
As a Systems Development Engineer on Data Services, you will design, build, and operate highly available services that model network devices, sites, and credentials, serving thousands of requests per second to automation workflows across the fulfillment network. You will build systems that collect the observed state of devices, including hardware inventory, firmware, interfaces, and neighbors, compare it against intended state, and surface drift before it causes customer impact. You will own data quality end to end, from schema design and validation at write time to staged, reviewable data changes, data health monitoring, and alarms that catch bad data before it reaches device configurations. You will lead migrations of legacy data sources onto modern APIs without disrupting the dozens of downstream teams that depend on them. You will take part in on-call, drive root-cause analysis and corrective actions, and turn recurring operational pain into automation, using AWS (CDK, Lambda, DynamoDB, S3, OpenSearch) and CI/CD pipelines to automate infrastructure and deployments.
Ideal candidates enjoy working where distributed systems meet network data. You communicate clearly, turn ambiguous requirements into simple, durable designs, and care as much about how a service runs in production as how it is built. You will work in a fast-moving, collaborative environment with partner teams who depend on your systems every day.
A day in the life
You will be a part of an agile development team following innovative best practices in software development where you will work on technical designs, architecture and coding. To build our applications, you will interact with network engineering teams to gather requirements, provide technical solutions and develop the software that are required in defining our next generation products.
Amazon offers a full range of benefits that assist you and eligible family members, including domestic partners. Benefits can vary by location, the number of regularly scheduled hours you work, length of employment, and job status such as seasonal or temporary employment. The benefits that generally apply to regular, full-time employees include:
Medical, Dental, and Vision Coverage
Maternity and Parental Leave Options
Paid Time Off (PTO)
401(k) Plan
If you are not sure that every qualification on the list above describes you exactly, we'd still love to hear from you! At Amazon, we value people with unique backgrounds, experiences, and skillsets. If you’re passionate about this role and want to make an impact on a global scale, please apply!
About The Team
Our team exists so that network engineers and automation teams can trust the data that runs Amazon's fulfillment network. We own the systems of record for network devices, sites, and credentials, plus the systems that observe what is actually running on devices in the field. Config generation, deployments, and lifecycle workflows across Imperium are all built on these services. We are accountable for making that data correct, fast, and safe to change, and we start from the customer: every bad record we prevent is an outage a network engineer never has to debug. As part of Data Services, you will work with automation, network engineering, and build teams across Amazon, and you will own your systems end to end, from design through operating them in production for hundreds of thousands of devices.

2+ years of non-internship professional software development experience

Strong C++ skills and a working knowledge of Kalman filtering, INS and GNSS.

Navigation software that has shipped on a fielded platform, not only in simulation.

Opportunity Summary
A venture-backed space startup is building modular spacecraft that dock and latch together in orbit using electromagnetic actuation, creating vehicles far larger than anything that fits inside a rocket fairing. Controlling a spacecraft whose mass, inertia, and shape change as it assembles is an open problem, and this team is solving it with flight hardware.
We are adding a talented early-career GNC engineer to a strong, senior controls team. You will work across attitude control, estimation, and nonlinear control of electromagnetic actuators, taking algorithms from simulation into flight software and hardware-in-the-loop testing. The bar is high, and in return you will get real ownership and direct mentorship from engineers who have flown GNC systems.
About Us
We are a venture-backed space technology startup in Golden, Colorado building modular spacecraft that launch as compact units and join together in orbit to form larger, more capable vehicles. The core technology has already flown in multiple on-orbit and microgravity demonstrations, and a newly outfitted facility is supporting the move toward larger hardware and a free-flying demonstration. The team is small and senior, with engineers who have shipped hardware at leading launch, satellite, and defense companies, and every engineer owns a real piece of the vehicle.
Job Duties
Develop attitude determination and control algorithms in C++ and Python for de-tumble, pointing, slewing, and momentum management
Model and control spacecraft whose inertia and structure change as modules join and separate
Design and tune nonlinear controllers for electromagnetic actuators used in docking and relative motion
Build simulations and run 6DOF Monte Carlo analyses to verify performance
Take algorithms into flight software and validate them through hardware-in-the-loop testing
Support sensor and actuator trade studies and help define GNC requirements
Support flight operations and on-orbit anomaly investigations

Bachelor's degree in aerospace, mechanical, or electrical engineering, physics, mathematics, or a related field
2+ years of professional or graduate research experience in controls, GNC, or dynamics
Strong grounding in control theory, including nonlinear control
Software development experience in C++ and Python
Track record that shows you are performing well ahead of your years of experience
Comfortable as a generalist who can pick up new areas quickly
U.S. person status (U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, refugee, or asylee) required under ITAR
Preferred Experience
Experience with electromagnets, electromagnetic actuators, or magnetic force and torque modeling
Graduate research (MS or PhD) in controls, electromagnetics, or related areas
Spacecraft ADCS experience, including attitude dynamics, quaternion kinematics, and state estimation such as MEKF
Experience with flexible-body or multi-body dynamics
Hardware-in-the-loop testing or real-world deployment of control algorithms
Experience with Git and collaborative software workflows
Why Join Us
Work on a GNC problem that has no textbook answer: controlling spacecraft that reconfigure in orbit
Learn directly from senior GNC engineers while owning meaningful parts of the system
Take your algorithms from simulation to flight hardware
Early-employee stock options with meaningful upside as the platform moves toward operational missions
Fast growth on a small team, where engineers who deliver take on broader ownership quickly

Short- and long-term disability insurance and life insurance

When the team decides whether a diagnostic has enough evidence to move from observation into blocking production, your data answers that question.
This is a software engineering role, not a reporting role. You will write and operate production code, own the alarms and metrics that page us, and build detection for trends nobody is watching yet. Experience with telemetry or diagnostic data from a large server fleet, or with defining metrics and anomaly detection on operational time-series data, will have you productive faster. Design, build, and operate production data pipelines that ingest diagnostic, telemetry, and repair-ticket data from the Trainium and Inferentia fleet into a warehouse other teams query with confidence.

Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.

You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.

Computer hardware and software engineers’ research, design, develop, and test computer hardware and software programs. Hardware refers to computer chips, circuit boards, computer systems, and related equipment such as keyboards, modems, and printers.

Computer software engineers apply the principles and techniques of computer science, engineering, and mathematical analysis to the design, development, testing, and evaluation of the software and systems that enable computers to perform their many applications.
Software engineers analyze users’ needs and design, construct, test, and maintain computer applications software or systems.

Software engineers must possess strong programming skills but are more concerned with developing algorithms and analyzing and solving programming problems than with actually writing code.

SambaNova is a leader in next-generation AI infrastructure, delivering a full-stack inference platform for customers worldwide. Its decode performance is especially strong for agentic workloads like multi-turn agents, code generation, and long-running applications. RDUs are packaged into SambaRack, rack-scale hardware that lets customers deploy state-of-the-art models with better performance, greater energy efficiency, and faster time to value.

The ML Infrastructure team builds and operates the inference stack that serves SambaNova's models on our RDU accelerators. We cover request scheduling, caching, decoding techniques, public APIs, and the accuracy testing that every inference feature must pass before it ships.

As a new grad ML Infrastructure Engineer, you'll write production Python for our inference serving stack, including our vLLM integration and public APIs. You'll help bring features like speculative decoding, prompt caching, and tool calling into production on the RDU, and add accuracy and regression tests that catch problems before customers do.

Implement inference features on the RDU such as speculative decoding, constrained decoding, tool calling, prompt caching, and long-context inference
Adapt vLLM and related serving frameworks to the RDU architecture
Build and maintain endpoints in the public inference API
Write accuracy verification and regression tests for inference features
Debug latency, throughput, and reliability issues in production services

Strong programming skills in Python
Understanding of algorithms, data structures, concurrency, and systems design
Coursework or project experience in distributed systems or machine learning
Experience with LLM serving frameworks such as vLLM, SGLang, or TensorRT-LLM
Experience with inference techniques such as speculative decoding, KV caching, or continuous batching
Experience with PyTorch
Preferred Qualifications
M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, or related field
Experience building or maintaining APIs or backend services
Internship or research experience in ML systems or backend infrastructure
Experience with disaggregated systems - prefill/decode
Open source project ownership or contributions

Who We Are
Nuro believes self-driving vehicles are the most immediate and profound opportunity for AI to drive positive change in the physical world. About The Role
Nuro operates real self-driving vehicles on public roads today — not a research platform, not ADAS. The Embedded Software Engineering team builds the software for the safety-critical embedded controllers that connect the Nuro Driver™ to the vehicle: the devices that command steering, braking, and propulsion, alongside other vehicle actuators, distribute and monitor power, monitor vehicle motion, and bring the vehicle to a safe state when something goes wrong.
As an Embedded Software Engineer, you will work across the full stack of multicore automotive microcontrollers from RTOS, drivers, and scheduler up through middleware and application components that talk to the vehicle, and help extend that stack as our hardware evolves. You will bring the Nuro Driver™ up on new vehicle platforms alongside OEM and supplier engineers, and see your code drive real vehicles on public roads. Integrate the Nuro Driver™ with new vehicle platforms: define and implement CAN and Ethernet interfaces with OEM ECUs, adapt actuator and body-control interfaces, and validate them on bench and in vehicle.
Take part in hands-on device and vehicle bring-up, prototyping and debugging on multiple vehicle platforms, from first power-on to autonomous driving.
Build and maintain the team's verification infrastructure: unit tests, hardware-in-the-loop benches and vehicle test procedures.
Work within an ISO 26262 development process: define software requirements from system safety requirements, then implement and verify them with full traceability.
Collaborate daily with systems, safety, hardware, controls and autonomy engineers, and with OEM and supplier partners, from definition through verification.

2+ years of industry experience developing embedded software in C, including work on a real-time operating system.
Solid computer science fundamentals: data structures, concurrency and algorithm design.
Working knowledge of microcontroller internals and peripherals, with depth in at least one of device driver development, CAN or automotive Ethernet, bootloaders and software update, embedded security, or vehicle-level integration and test.
Strong problem-solving and debugging skills, clear written and spoken communication, and a track record of working well with engineers from other disciplines.
Comfortable at the bench with debug probes, oscilloscopes, logic analyzers and CAN tools. You enjoy finding out why hardware and software disagree.
Bonus Points
3+ years of embedded development in the automotive or autonomous vehicle industry, including a production launch.
Hands-on functional safety experience with ISO 26262, or safety-critical development in another regulated industry such as DO-178C or IEC 62304.
Experience with Infineon AURIX TC3xx, SafeRTOS or FreeRTOS, or AUTOSAR Classic base software such as MCAL and communication stacks.
Vehicle network integration experience: DBC and ARXML, UDS diagnostics, E2E protection, time synchronization.
Knowledge of vehicle functions, vehicle dynamics or control theory.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.
About The Team
The Imaging team builds and fields state-of-the-art camera and sensor systems deployed to solve real security challenges for the United States and its allies. We work across the full stack, from bare-metal hardware and firmware to networked services and cloud integrations, and we own our systems all the way through to the field. When something breaks in a deployed environment, we fix it.
About The Role
We're looking for a Mission Software Engineer to join the Imaging Interfaces team. This is not a pure product development role. You will spend meaningful time keeping fielded systems alive, triaging issues across the full stack, and serving as a technical representative for our products in integrations with external teams and customers.
The work is varied and sometimes ambiguous. You might spend a morning extending a gRPC service, an afternoon diagnosing a time sync issue on a deployed device over the phone with a field operator, and a week traveling to support a customer integration. You'll need to be comfortable with that range--and ideally energized by it.
If you want to own your software end-to-end in a fast-moving environment where the stakes are real, this role is built for you.
What You'll Do
Own fielded system success.
You are responsible for the health and uptime of deployed imaging systems. When issues arise--whether the root cause is in your code, the firmware, the network, or the hardware--you triage, diagnose, and drive resolution.
Build and maintain production services.
You'll develop and extend modular software services that run on edge-compute devices in austere environments. These services need to be reliable, observable, and maintainable by engineers who didn't write them.
Support field operations.
You'll work directly with field operators and non-technical users to diagnose and resolve issues on deployed hardware. Clear communication under pressure is part of the job.
Represent the team externally.
You'll serve as a subject matter expert in integrations with other products and teams; sometimes remotely, sometimes on-site. You don't need to know everything, but you need to be able to speak credibly across the full system stack and know what you don't know.
Maintain end-to-end system understanding.
Our devices sit at the intersection of hardware, firmware, networking, and software. You'll develop broad fluency across that stack over time, and apply it to optimize how our services interact and degrade gracefully when components fail.
Collaborate across teams.
You'll plan, build, and test complex functionality alongside firmware, hardware, and platform engineers. You'll need to be effective working across team and organizational boundaries.
Travel expected approximately 25% of the time for field testing and customer integrations.
What We're Looking For
Required
2+ years of software development with meaningful production ownership: not just shipping features, but owning systems after they ship (their health, uptime, and behavior once they are in users' hands).
Deep proficiency in at least one of C++, TypeScript(node.js/React), or Python, and the ability to work effectively across the stack boundary in a second language (reading, debugging, and modifying code outside your primary). Our work spans a large TypeScript/React operator-facing UI and a growing body of C++ services running on edge hardware, and C++ depth is increasingly central as we expand across our imaging product lines.
Comfort ramping quickly into unfamiliar languages, tools, and deployment systems. Our language and tooling mix varies by product and shifts over time; we value engineers who get productive in a new stack rather than staying in one lane.
2+ years working in Linux-based environments, including hands-on work with bare-metal hardware.
Demonstrated ability to diagnose and resolve issues across system boundaries (networking, services, hardware interaction) without always having full visibility into every component.
Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain technical problems clearly to non-technical audiences, including operators in the field.
Eligibility to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance.
Preferred
Strength with performance-sensitive, real-time, or resource-constrained systems (edge or embedded).
Experience with gRPC or similar RPC frameworks.
Familiarity with systemd service management and observability practices on Linux.
Familiarity with Nix or NixOS: uncommon, but genuinely valuable, and something you will use daily on our stack.
Experience supporting fielded or deployed systems, not just development environments.

ABOUT NIRVA
Nirva is building the first AI fashion accessory for your mind — a necklace or bracelet that privately listens only to the wearer to enable proactive journaling, emotion tracking, and life coaching. Think Oura Ring for your Mind.
Backed by Lightspeed and South Park Commons, recognized at CES within 90 days of founding, and launching in the U.S. this fall. Co-founders bring backgrounds from Meta Reality Labs (Quest, Ray-Ban glasses) and fashion industry.
THE ROLE
We’re looking for an AI Audio / Voice Engineer to build the audio front door to Nirva’s intelligence layer: the systems that capture only the wearer, reliably, privately, and with as much processing on device as possible. This is the trust foundation for the whole product. If Nirva cannot tell who is speaking, reject everyone else, and do it in noisy real life without draining the battery or sending raw audio where it should not go, nothing built on top of it works. You will own voiceprint, on-device audio, and the technical systems behind our privacy promise, and work directly with the founding team to build them from the ground up.
WHAT YOU'LL OWN
Voiceprint: build speaker enrollment, voice embeddings, verification and identification so Nirva recognizes the wearer and separates them from bystanders, family, coworkers, and media
Tune and evaluate voiceprint in the real world: false accepts, false rejects, noisy cafes, walking, wind, cars, quiet rooms, illness, and voice drift over time, plus re-enrollment and recovery flows
Anti-spoofing and trust protections: replay and impersonation resistance, liveness signals where relevant, and clear fallbacks when confidence is low
On-device audio: design the on-device pipeline for voice activity detection, segmentation, speaker filtering, audio preprocessing, noise suppression, and streaming to speech recognition, with tight latency, power, thermal, and memory budgets
Decide the on-device vs. cloud split for each audio task and build graceful fallbacks when connectivity, battery, or confidence changes
Trust by design: on-device first processing, bystander exclusion, consent and recording controls, encryption in transit and at rest, data minimization, retention and deletion controls, and user-visible controls that match what the system actually does
Build evals and data pipelines for audio: test sets across people, accents, environments, and devices, failure analysis, and systematic debugging of real user-facing failures
Partner with product, design, and the memory / AI teams so clean, trusted, wearer-only audio becomes transcripts, memories, and experiences users can rely on

2+ years of full-time engineering experience, or a PhD in computer science, electrical engineering, machine learning, speech / audio, or a related field, plus 2 applied internships (industry or applied research) where you shipped or evaluated real systems

Hands-on experience with speech and audio ML in production: speaker embeddings, diarization, VAD, streaming audio, speech-to-text interfaces, audio preprocessing, or speech event detection
Experience running ML on device or at the edge: model quantization, distillation, latency and power optimization, and working within hardware constraints
Strong eval mindset for audio: you can build a test set, measure false accept / false reject and word error tradeoffs, find why a failure happened, and improve the system, not just the demo
Strong product engineering instincts and high ownership: you identify what needs to happen and drive it to shipped quality
Comfortable with ambiguous, human-centered problems where “good” is not easy to measure, and energized by 0-to-1 work, fast iteration, and early-stage startup intensity
Based in San Francisco and able to work in person

Shipped always-on or low-power audio, wearables, hearables, or mobile audio products
Experience with anti-spoofing, voice liveness, or biometric security and its failure modes
iOS audio, Core ML, or embedded / DSP experience
Privacy engineering, on-device personal data systems, or consumer trust and safety for sensing products

About Us
Preference Model is a superintelligence data research company. We build RL environments for training capable, better-aligned superintelligences.
Almost every aspect of how a model behaves is shaped by the reward signals it's trained on. The biggest problem with AIs today is that they don't always do what we intend. Sometimes that's because they aren't capable enough, and sometimes it's because they aren't aligned. Both problems come down to the training objectives.
We're trying to address both of these issues in the most direct, highest leverage way available to us, which today means researching how to build RL environments better, not just for the AIs of today but for the AIs as they will be when they outsmart us.
Over the past year, we've built RL environments for several frontier labs, and we're backed by $16M in seed funding led by a16z. Our founding team has previous experience on Anthropic’s data team building data infrastructure, and datasets behind Claude.
About The Role
An RL environment is only useful once it runs reliably inside a lab's training stack. Every environment we build has to be packaged, sandboxed, run at scale, checked against each lab's requirements, and delivered in the format that lab's platform expects. Much of that work is still manual today, and it takes time away from the people designing environments.
As an
MTS on our ML Platform team
, you will own the systems that take an environment from a builder's repo to a lab's training run. That includes Karotte, our open-source framework for defining RL environments, the internal platform that builds, runs, and reviews environments on CPU, GPU, and TPU, and the integrations that deliver them to each lab we work with. This is an engineering role where you will ensure what our Capabilities team builds runs and ships cleanly.
You'll join a small Platform team and work directly with environment builders and post-training researchers. In your first six months, success looks like a delivery path to each partner lab that is mostly automated: tasks marked ready get built, validated against that lab's requirements, and packaged without hand work. Our needs change quickly, so you'll also pick up other platform and infrastructure work as priorities shift.
What You Will Do
Own the integrations that deliver our environments to partner labs: build container images, match each lab's submission format, and automate the checks that confirm requirements are met before anything ships. Do the delivery work by hand where you have to, then automate it.
Build and maintain Karotte, our open-source environment framework, from API design through releases and migrations that keep existing environments working.
Run and scale the infrastructure that builds, runs, and grades environments, including containerized rollouts and grading across CPU, GPU, and TPU, VM-based sandboxing, and the resource limits and isolation that stop a model from gaming its own grader.
Build the internal tools environment builders use every day (CLI, docs, data catalog, access controls, and run monitoring) so they spend their time on environment design instead of infrastructure.
Partner with environment builders and post-training researchers to turn recurring pain points into platform features, and ship quickly in response to their feedback.
What We are Looking For
Strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of building and operating production infrastructure or developer platforms that other engineers depend on.
Proficiency in Python, including writing libraries and APIs that other people build on.
Hands-on experience with containers and orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes, or similar) and at least one major cloud platform (GCP, AWS, or similar).
A working understanding of how to run untrusted code safely: isolation, resource limits, and what happens when a process fills the disk or refuses to exit.
Extensive hands-on use of coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or similar), and an intuition for where models cut corners.
You've owned something tedious end to end, such as a migration, a release process, or a delivery pipeline, and automated away as much of it as you could.
Nice to Have
Experience building RL environments, eval harnesses, or agent benchmarks (Terminal-Bench, SWE-bench, or similar).
Familiarity with RL post-training and inference stacks (verl, Ray, SkyPilot, vLLM, SGLang, or similar).
You may be a good fit if one of the following applies
You've built sandbox or code-execution infrastructure (microVMs such as Firecracker, gVisor, or similar) at an infrastructure startup or frontier lab.
You've been an early platform or infrastructure engineer at a startup and built the internal platform the rest of engineering relied on.
You've worked as a forward deployed or integrations engineer, getting your company's software running inside customers' own environments.
You've built developer tooling or internal platforms used by ML researchers, even outside a formal ML role.
You've maintained an open-source developer framework with real external users.
What we offer:
Competitive cash and equity compensation (>90th percentile)
Ownership and autonomy in a fast moving startup environment
Opportunity to work alongside senior and staff engineers from frontier labs and infrastructure companies, plus top ML engineers
Health, vision, dental, benefits
401K match
Lunch provided everyday onsite
Weekly snack orders
Visa sponsorship & relocation support available
We value diverse perspectives and experiences. If you're excited about this role but don't check every box, we still encourage you to apply.

Motivo is a project-based company delivering excellence in mechanical and electrical system design and prototype builds. We are looking for a passionate, enthusiastic multidisciplinary engineer, capable of leading the technical decision-making process in electro-mechanical projects that require a solid system architecture.
What is a Systems Engineer? At Motivo, these are some of our most highly valued and versatile team members. The ideal Systems Engineer is someone who understands what it takes to execute on an electromechanical project from concept to fabrication. People with those skills are often creative, balance competing priorities well, and have a high degree of attention to detail. A Systems Engineer typically works with a Project Manager and Technical Lead to guide a focused team of engineers into the beginning phases of a product development program. Together, this group is responsible for planning the technical and programmatic aspects of the development, defining or reviewing the complete system architecture, identifying key components and technologies, and leading the technical team to successful project completion. Often, in later phases of the program, the Systems Engineer will lead brainstorms, review the work of other engineers, provide guidance along specific technical paths, and help debug and troubleshoot during integration.
A strong Systems Engineer candidate will know enough about mechanical, electrical, and software engineering, as well as physics in general, to speak intelligently about all of them and understand their interactions. The Motivo Systems Engineer position is the ideal role for an exceedingly sharp engineer who is insatiably curious about all aspects of engineering!

Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline (Master’s preferred)

Direct technical experience on multiple electro-mechanical projects
Deep understanding of physics and electro-mechanical control systems
Extensive detailed design experience in either mechanical, electrical or software systems

Simulation and controls development (we use Matlab/Simulink)
SPICE platforms for electronics simulation
3D CAD (we use Solidworks)
PCB design (we use Altium)
C/C++ for firmware development (we typically use STM32 MCUs for custom embedded hardware)
Higher-level software development (Python and C/C++ most often)

Ability to generate technical drawings of systems, components, and interfaces
Experience with troubleshooting, debugging, and root cause analysis of issues in electromechanical systems
Soft Skills And Experiences
Exceptional communication skills; able to present results and recommendations to internal and external stakeholders
Strong ability to lead and support a team of engineers through technical challenges
Solutions and execution focused; ability to make trades against competing priorities
Open to new ideas and challenges from the team
Reacts well to changing client needs
Ability to mentor less experienced colleagues
Ability to handle concurrent fast-paced projects with minimal direction
Exceptional English speaking ability and good-for-an-engineer writing skills
Positive, solutions-oriented attitude

We’re convinced that the team and the projects are hands-down the best part of working at Motivo. Job Description
The Systems Integration & Test Engineer performs hands-on integration, verification, testing, and troubleshooting of high-criticality avionics embedded systems. You will investigate product issues, validate system behavior, and provide technical guidance across multiple engineering disciplines.

Integrate, test, and troubleshoot high-criticality avionics embedded systems to ensure reliable operation.

Diagnose electrical, electronic, and system-level product issues and propose effective solutions.
Provide technical guidance on electrical functionality, system performance, and overall product behavior.
Develop, execute, and document detailed integration and verification test procedures.
Analyze test results, identify discrepancies, and clearly document findings for engineering review.
Reproduce reported product failures and assist in root-cause analysis and corrective-action investigations.
Use electrical schematics and technical documentation to isolate hardware, software, interface, and system-level problems.
Collaborate closely with electrical, software, systems, test, and specialty-engineering teams throughout the product lifecycle.
Support issue resolution and product updates across the systems engineering lifecycle.
Maintain accurate test records, problem reports, and verification evidence in accordance with engineering standards.
Essential Skills
Strong ability to diagnose electrical and system-level problems involving electronic equipment.
Ability to provide clear technical guidance related to product, electrical, or system functionality.
Ability to interpret electrical schematics, technical specifications, and test documentation.
Strong analytical and hands-on troubleshooting skills for complex electronic and embedded systems.
Ability to work effectively across hardware, software, systems, and test engineering disciplines.
Capability to perform verification activities against defined functional requirements.
Ability to work onsite in Endicott, NY.
Additional Skills & Qualifications
Experience with avionics or electronic control-system development.
Experience integrating and verifying electronic equipment that contains both hardware and embedded software.
Familiarity with avionics interfaces, communication protocols, or data buses.
Experience supporting high-reliability or safety-critical products.
Experience developing or executing system-level verification procedures.
Experience using standard laboratory equipment such as oscilloscopes, digital multimeters, logic analyzers, signal generators, or protocol analyzers.
Familiarity with failure investigation, root-cause analysis, and corrective-action processes.
Experience documenting test results and technical findings in a regulated engineering environment.

This position is based onsite in Endicott, NY, in a laboratory and engineering environment focused on high-criticality avionics and electronic control systems. Ready to join a mission that matters? The future of cybersecurity starts with you.
About The Role:
CrowdStrike Falcon is a two-component security product. One component is the "Sensor" — a lightweight agent installed on endpoint systems that observes system activity, recognizes malicious behavior, provides on-box prevention capability, and sends telemetry to the Falcon cloud. The cloud component aggregates Sensor telemetry across each customer's network, correlates malicious behavior across machines, and presents security teams with a prioritized summary of the threats detected in their environments.
The Falcon Sensor runs on tens of millions of endpoints worldwide, across Windows, macOS and Linux, in both user mode and kernel mode. Engineering software at that depth and that scale is among the hardest problems in the industry, and CrowdStrike holds the Sensor to an exceptionally high standard of quality, performance and engineering rigor. Sustaining that standard requires a team with true mastery of what software does at runtime, at the lowest levels of the stack.
That team is Sensor Performance and Reliability — CrowdStrike's team of debug engineers. Deep runtime analysis is our craft: postmortem memory dump analysis, disassembly and reverse engineering, and source-level analysis, used to explain with precision and evidence how low-level code behaves on real systems. It is one of the most technically demanding specialties in systems engineering, and very few organizations invest in it as a discipline in its own right. We do, because at our scale the answer to "what exactly happened, and why?" has to be exact rather than approximate.
Our mandate goes further than answering that question well. We're chartered to turn what we learn from deep analysis into durable engineering improvements — strengthening diagnostics, tooling, validation coverage and development practices so that lessons generalize far beyond the investigation that produced them, and so that the next analysis is faster than the last. Our work makes the product stronger, and it raises the engineering capability of every team we work with.
We are hiring an entry-level engineer to join us in that mission. We do not expect you to arrive with deep Windows internals, assembly, or reverse engineering experience. Those are skills we will teach you, and you will learn them from engineers who operate at the top of this field. What we are looking for is a strong programmer with excellent problem-solving instincts and genuine curiosity about how computers actually work underneath the abstractions — someone who is drawn to a hard, ambiguous problem rather than put off by it. If you are the kind of person who cannot leave a mystery alone until you understand it completely, this is an unusually good place to build a career.

Analyze the runtime behavior of complex low-level software across user mode and kernel mode on Windows, primarily through postmortem memory dump analysis in WinDbg.
Work from raw memory, register state and disassembly to a precise, evidence-backed account of what executing code did and why — and hold yourself to a high evidentiary bar in reaching it.

https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/44844.description_preview:
Who we are
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone’s reach while doing the most important work of your career.
About The Team
Radar helps businesses prevent payments fraud and abuse while enabling legitimate customers to transact with confidence. We combine machine learning and AI with the intelligence of Stripe’s global network to make sophisticated fraud prevention accessible to businesses of all sizes.
Our work spans payments fraud detection, protection against abuse beyond the payment, enterprise APIs that bring Radar’s capabilities into businesses’ own systems and payment flows, and the platform that powers it all. We build everything from reliable, low-latency infrastructure to intuitive tools that help users understand threats and control how they respond.
Fraud evolves constantly, and so do we. We work directly with users to understand emerging attacks, turn advances in ML and AI into effective defenses, and build products that protect and grow their revenue.
What you’ll do
As a software engineer on Radar, you’ll build products and infrastructure that help businesses understand and stop fraud and abuse. Your work will span backend services, enterprise APIs, and user experiences that put sophisticated prevention capabilities into our customers’ hands.
You’ll own problems from investigation through launch, partnering with product managers, designers, and data scientists. You’ll have opportunities to scale systems that make real-time decisions across Stripe’s global payments network, bring advances in ML and AI into production, and build new products from scratch. Every improvement can have a direct impact on the revenue our users retain and the legitimate customers they serve.
Responsibilities
Build and operate reliable, low-latency services that detect and prevent fraud and abuse at scale
Design APIs and dashboard experiences that help businesses investigate threats, configure defenses, and understand how Radar protects them
Develop the shared platform and infrastructure that enable teams to build and launch new Radar capabilities
Work directly with users to understand emerging threats and turn those insights into broadly useful products
Partner with ML engineers and data scientists to bring new signals, models, and AI capabilities into production
Own projects end to end, from technical design and implementation through rollout, measurement, and iteration
Uphold a high bar for engineering quality, reliability, and product craft while moving quickly as threats evolve
Who you are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.
Minimum Requirements
2+ years of industry software engineering experience
Strong coding skills in any programming language, with experience building and maintaining production software
Ability to work across systems and technologies, learn unfamiliar codebases, and make thoughtful technical trade-offs
A rigorous approach to problem solving, including using data to investigate issues and evaluate whether a solution works
Strong collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to work across disciplines and contribute to your peers’ success
An ownership mindset and comfort navigating ambiguity, taking initiative, and following through on user problems
Preferred Qualifications
Experience building distributed systems or real-time services with demanding reliability and latency requirements
Experience building APIs, developer platforms, or intuitive user interfaces for complex workflows
Experience bringing ML or AI capabilities into production software
Experience working on fraud prevention, abuse prevention, risk, or security
Experience taking a product from an early idea to launch and iterating directly with customers
Hybrid work at Stripe
This role is available either in an office or a remote location (35+ miles or 56+ km from a Stripe office).
In-office expectations
Office-assigned Stripes spend at least 50% of the time in a given month in their local office or with users. This hits a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility about how to do this in a way that makes sense for individuals and their teams.
Working remotely at Stripe
A remote location is defined as being 35 miles (56 kilometers) or more from one of our offices. While you would be welcome to come into the office for team/business meetings, on-sites, meet-ups, and events, our expectation is you would regularly work from home rather than a Stripe office. Stripe does not cover the cost of relocating to a remote location. We encourage you to apply for roles that match the location where you currently live or plan to live.

About The Role

You will work on a small, highly focused team building production-quality software that enables efficient and accurate creation of HD maps at Cyngn deployment-sites and robust localization for Cyngn’s autonomous vehicle fleets.

This role is a strong fit for an early-career engineer who has solid robotics fundamentals and is eager to deepen their expertise in mapping and localization on real production hardware.
What You'll Do
Implement, tune, and test mapping, localization, and sensor calibration algorithms for our autonomous vehicle platforms using C++ and Python, with guidance and code review from senior team members.

Debug and analyze algorithm performance using real-world and simulated sensor data, and iterate based on results from vehicle testing.
Balance assigned project tasks, code reviews, and learning to meet product-driven milestones in a fast-paced startup environment.
Qualifications
BS or MS in robotics, computer science, electrical engineering, or a similar technical field (MS a plus).
Solid foundation in probability theory, linear algebra, 3D geometry, and spatial coordinate transformations.

Have agents flag low confidence or missing data and hand off to a person.

Company Overview
Our company is a start-up that specializes in episodes of care benefit plans. We have a deep expertise in episode pricing and analytics and our goal is to bring transparency and efficiency to the healthcare market. Our company is committed to providing high-quality, affordable healthcare to our customers.
Role Description
The Data Integration Engineer for Healthcare Transactions is a hands-on software engineer responsible for designing, building, and operating the data pipelines and integrations that move healthcare data, including claims, enrollment, and other transactions, into and out of the organization's systems. This is an individual contributor role on the engineering team: this person writes the code, mappings, and tests behind each feed, deploys it to production, and owns its reliability from there. The ideal candidate is an engineer who knows healthcare data standards in detail and treats integrations as production software.
Responsibilities
Design, build, test, and deploy inbound and outbound data pipelines with providers, payers, vendors, and network partners, covering Claims and Billing files, Provider Directory files, NPPES, ICD10 and other data sources.
Write the parsing, mapping, and transformation logic in Python and SQL that validates, normalizes, and loads partner data into internal data models.
Build and maintain the APIs and services that move integrated data into billing and other core systems.
Build automated data quality checks, validation rules, and exception handling so bad or incomplete files are caught before they reach downstream systems or clients.
Instrument pipelines with logging, monitoring, and alerting; investigate production failures, perform root cause analysis, and ship fixes that keep issues from recurring.
Build reusable components and templates that make each new feed faster to stand up than the last.
Optimize pipelines for performance and cost as data volumes and the number of partners grow.
Apply HIPAA and security requirements in code and infrastructure, including encryption, secure file transfer, access controls, and audit logging.
Own the technical side of new client and partner connections end to end: review file specifications, build and test the feed, run test cycles with the partner, and move to production.
Work directly with technical contacts at clients and vendors to troubleshoot data issues and agree on file layouts and requirements (e.g., custom 837 claims, 834 enrollment files).
Work with Product, account management, and operations teams to turn business requirements into technical designs with clear acceptance criteria.
Surface integration pain points and edge cases to inform the product and engineering roadmap.
Follow the team's software development practices, including version control, code review, automated testing, and CI/CD deployments.
Write and maintain technical specifications, mapping documents, and runbooks so integrations can be supported and extended by other engineers.
Qualifications
Describe the experience and attributes of the ideal candidate
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Healthcare Informatics, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
3+ years of hands-on software or data engineering experience building and supporting production data integrations, preferably within the healthcare sector (payer or health plan experience a plus).
Strong proficiency in Python and SQL.
Working knowledge of healthcare transaction standards, especially X12 837 and 834; experience with 835, 270/271, HL7, or FHIR a plus.
Experience building data pipelines on AWS (e.g., S3, Lambda).
Experience with RESTful APIs, JSON, and SFTP-based file exchange.
Experience with Git, automated testing, and CI/CD pipelines.
Experience with an integration engine or orchestration tool (e.g., Mirth Connect, Rhapsody, InterSystems, Airflow) a plus.
Understanding of HIPAA requirements for handling protected health information.
Strong debugging and problem-solving skills, and clear written and verbal communication, including with external technical contacts.
Benefits
Health: Medical, dental, and vision insurance
Retirement: 401(k) with company match
Paid leave: Vacation, Sick, and company holidays
Ancillary: Company-paid life and disability insurance

About Us
Mintive helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools.
Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. Our gateway product scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on.
We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how.
We are AI-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them.
Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co-founded Coursera.
The Job
You will own features end to end, from conception to production, across our gateway infrastructure, enterprise deployments, and agentic systems. The work leans backend and infra, but nothing is off limits: when the product needs a better UI you build it, and when a connector breaks during a security review you fix it.
Claude and Codex are your primary working environment, and you use a fleet of agents to move faster than a team this size has any right to. Agents write much of the code and review PRs, so your real job is the judgment they cannot make: shaping the problem, making architecture, product, and UX calls, hardening enterprise paths, designing connectors, protecting security-sensitive surfaces, and catching generated code that is quietly wrong. Roles are blurred and we ship within hours, and you will learn directly from the founders and from customers.
We hire across levels, from strong early-career builders to seasoned engineers, and we set level and pay to match. What matters most is judgment, range, and how fast you ship.
About You
You are a builder with a track record of shipping to real users, whether that is a product, an internal tool, an open-source project, or a serious side project. You ship, then iterate, without waiting for specs or approvals.
You have strong fundamentals and learn fast. How quickly you pick things up matters as much as years of experience.
You care about product value and customer needs over technical purity.
You take infra seriously. You think about blast radius, trust boundaries, and what happens when your code is in the path of every customer's agents.
You can read unfamiliar code, reason from first principles, and explain your tradeoffs.
You are comfortable across the stack (TypeScript, Python, CockroachDB), or you pick up new languages, protocols, and domains fast.
You are excited to build with agents, and to learn when they help and when they hide a problem.
You already build with AI every day and want room to move without heavy process.
Nice to have:
Developer-facing products, protocol or gateway work, or infrastructure at scale.
Background in security, identity, or permission systems.
Contributions to open source, MCP servers, or agentic frameworks.
Design sensibility: engineers who care about design, designers who think about infrastructure.
What we offer:
Competitive compensation and meaningful equity.
Unusual scope and ownership of features that ship to enterprise customers.
Building and deploying agents on the same platform we sell.
Direct access to the founders, customer context, and product direction, with mentorship as you grow.
Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first.

Spanning software and platform, reliability, quality, cyber security, service operations, service management, financial engineering and data science, these roles work across the full lifecycle to solve complex problems, enable secure and resilient delivery, and drive continuous improvement in a product-led, data-driven environment.
Software & Platform Engineering
Roles in Software & Platform Engineering focus on building and improving the software, infrastructure and systems that support our products and services. Engineers work across the full software and infrastructure lifecycle to deliver usable, maintainable applications.
Reliability Engineering
Roles in the Reliability Engineering track play a crucial role in identifying and reducing risks to performance and availability. They develop tools and implement strategies to prevent problems before they occur and recover quickly from a failure keeping platforms, applications, and services stable and reliable.
During the recruitment process we will get to know your skills and interest and how they align with the needs of the business to place you in your Engineering Team.
What We Are Looking For
We are passionate about recruiting people who have a genuine curiosity about Technology and strive to pursue a Technology career path, as evidenced by their studies, extracurriculars or work experience. It’s important to us that you can also understand the breadth of our organisation, how it functions and the vital role that technology plays in supporting LSEG and our clients.
You will have a strong interest in technology proven either via your work experience, extracurricular activities, or academic studies. For instance, you may have secured an internship in a technology role or focused on technology as part of a university project. You may have learnt how to code or how to use a particular technology.
You should have a demonstrable interest in financial markets, which you’ve built through your studies, work experience or extracurricular activities.
A curiosity for data and an ability to analyse information to draw conclusions and propose solutions.
Individuals who can connect the dots and think strategically.
The environment we work in is fast paced, you’ll need to demonstrate focus, resilience and the flexibility to adapt to changing demands.
People who can collaborate with others, using their communication skills in the process.
Ideal candidates will have the rights to work in the US without restrictions for the duration of the graduate programme and joins us on a permanent basis from day one.
We value not just what you achieve, but how you achieve it.
We are considering candidates beyond the core software degrees (e.g. computer science, software engineering, Mathematics and Informatics) and candidate with physics, engineering, electronic degree who can demonstrate an interest in Technology as evidenced by extracurriculars or work experience, or personal projects can apply.
Application close:
20th October
, however we recommend an early application because we consider candidates on a rolling basis. Due to the volume of applications, we might close the applications earlier, so we recommend an early application.
Recruitment Process:
The first stage of the recruitment process involves making an application and submitting your resume.
The second stage is completing Technical and Coding Assessment.
The third stage of the application process is an Immersive Online Assessment. The assessment is designed to give you an insight into what it’s like to work at LSEG.
The fourth stage is a video interview where you will answer a series of questions using a strength-based-interview style.
The final stage is a half day assessment centre which involves several different types of exercises – further information is provided at the point of invite.

Description
Amazon Leo is closing the digital divide with a constellation of 3,236 low-Earth-orbit (LEO) satellites bringing fast, affordable broadband to communities the internet has never reliably reached. The customer terminal is the phased-array antenna at the customer's premises that turns that constellation into a working internet link — and our team writes the embedded software that makes it work: acquiring a LEO satellite on a fast overhead pass, electronically steering the beam to track it, closing and holding the link, and handing over to the next satellite within seconds. This is a broad role — you can work across the full signal chain and go deep wherever interests you most.
What You'll Work On
Electronic beam steering & tracking — real-time control that keeps a phased-array beam pointed at a fast-moving satellite across the pass and through every handover.
Phased-array calibration — per-element amplitude/phase calibration that holds beam and sidelobe performance across unit-to-unit variation, temperature, and frequency, on real hardware in the field, with the automated test coverage to keep it reliable.
Link acquisition, tracking & management — satellite acquisition, closed-loop tracking, and the control that brings the link up, keeps it healthy, and reacquires cleanly through handovers.
RF power & thermal management — managing transmit power and duty cycle against PA and platform thermal limits so the terminal runs at full performance without exceeding its envelope.
System integration & field telemetry — integrate the RF front-end, controls, and signal path, then use device telemetry to debug and improve terminals operating on orbit.
Key job responsibilities
What We Look For
Embedded C/C++ or Rust on Linux/RTOS, close to the hardware.
Wireless / RF / DSP exposure — phased arrays, beamforming, SatCom, 5G/LTE, radar, or similar — or strong drive to grow into it.
Hands-on hardware debugging — comfortable with lab instruments, RF test setups, and reading telemetry to reason about a live system.
Our Stack
Rust, C/C++, and Python on embedded Linux / RTOS, working directly with the RF front-end and real hardware — lab terminals, RF test benches, and satellites on orbit. Automated hardware-in-the-loop testing and rich fleet telemetry let you see the impact of your code in the real world. New development is increasingly in Rust.

is building a horizontal identity platform

The old approach doesn’t hold up. It’s either IT teams duct-taping systems together, or rigid IGA tools that only work across a narrow set of HR and SSO integrations. That’s not going to cut it for the next decade.
We’re building something more foundational: a horizontal identity platform that any company—and increasingly, any AI agent—can plug into to understand and manage access. SaaS apps, infrastructure, internal tools, AI agents—if it has a concept of “who,” it should connect to us.
We’re still small, and we move fast. If you want to help build this from the ground up, you’ll have real ownership here.

and
shipping, often in the same session, with agentic development as a core part of how you work.

why
something should exist and
how
it should work, and you can move from that clarity to a working implementation quickly.

Design and build product experiences end to end, from problem framing through working implementation.
Work across a modern, AI-native toolkit every day: agentic coding harnesses, design tools like Paper and Pen.dev, prototyping tools like Claude Design, and MCP integrations that connect them. Use whatever gets you from idea to artifact fastest.
Make design decisions grounded in data. Draw on research and specs from product designers and product managers, and use tools to pull signal from usage, support, and customer feedback yourself, then translate what you find into solutions.
Contribute to and evolve our design system, ensuring consistency and quality as the product surface area grows.
Work directly in code to prototype, validate, and ship UI. Not as a novelty, but as your default mode.
Communicate the why behind design decisions clearly and publicly. We design in the open here.
Collaborate closely with engineering and product to maintain quality at speed.
